claims.text: FeB-based components with a standard boride microstructure are prone to corrosion during molten-aluminum exposure.
A thin CrN diffusion barrier with a graded adhesion interlayer will significantly improve the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of FeB-based components at approximately 660°C.
The proposed coating consists of 100–200 nm of CrN deposited by PVD.
The proposed coating includes a graded Cr or CrSi interfacial layer.
A graded Cr or CrSi interfacial layer will enhance adhesion of the CrN coating to the FeB-based substrate.
Brief post-annealing will improve coating integrity.
The proposed deposition temperature is approximately 500°C, followed by post-annealing and testing in molten aluminum at approximately 660°C.
The treatment will produce a dense, defect-free CrN coating.
The graded adhesion interlayer will minimize the effects of thermal-expansion mismatch and keep the barrier intact during thermal cycling.
CrN is chemically inert under the proposed molten-aluminum operating conditions.
The CrN layer will prevent or reduce interdiffusion and direct interfacial reactions between the FeB substrate and molten aluminum.
The graded adhesion layer will mitigate thermal stresses and prevent cracks that would compromise the CrN barrier.
Coated FeB-based components will have significantly lower corrosion-related weight loss than uncoated FeB-based components.
Coated FeB-based components will exhibit less interfacial degradation than uncoated components.
The coating treatment will extend component service life under molten-aluminum conditions.
Uncoated FeB-based components typically undergo rapid corrosion and interfacial degradation during molten-aluminum plating.
The intervention is expected to remain effective for FeB-based systems under plating conditions near 660°C.
Existing literature supports high chemical stability of CrN coatings.
